st: Place the salt cod in a bowl, cover with cold water, and soak in the fridge for several hours, changing the water 2 to 3 times.
Drain the cod, put it in a pot of fresh water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes to remove excess salt.
Drain the cod, let it cool a little, then flake it into bite-size pieces and remove any bones or skin.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and [[1 cup]] water, then simmer for 10 minutes until they break down into a sauce.
Add the flaked cod, the whole hot pepper if using, and [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 10 minutes so the fish absorbs the flavors. Taste before adding any salt, since the cod is already salty.
Remove the thyme stems and hot pepper and serve hot with rice, boiled dumplings, or breadfruit.
Peel the plantains by cutting off both ends and slicing through the skin lengthwise, then lifting it off.
Slice the plantains on a slant into pieces about 0.5 inch thick.
Mix [[1 tsp]] chili flakes, [[0.5 tsp]] paprika, [[0.5 tsp]] garlic powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a small bowl.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat until a plantain slice sizzles right away.
Fry the slices in a single layer for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden brown. Work in batches.
Move the fried plantains to a plate lined with paper towels.
While still hot, sprinkle with the spice mix and toss to coat.
Serve warm with lime wedges.
Whisk [[2 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] baking powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt together in a large bowl.
Rub in [[3 tbsp]] cold butter with your fingertips until the mix looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] coconut and [[3 tbsp]] sugar.
Add about [[0.5 cup]] cold water a little at a time and mix until a firm dough forms. Knead briefly for 1 minute.
Rest the dough, covered, for 15 minutes.
Bring [[6 cups]] water to a rolling boil in a large pot with a pinch of salt.
Shape the dough into 8 to 10 ovals or fat rounds, slightly flattened.
Drop them into the boiling water, lower to a steady simmer, and cook for 15 minutes until they float and feel firm.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and serve warm with stews or stewed fish.
Season the goat with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the goat in batches for about 8 minutes total.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, cloves and hot pepper and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes collapse.
Pour in [[8 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer and cover.
Simmer for 1.5 hours, skimming foam from the top, until the goat is very tender.
Add the breadfruit or potatoes and cook 15 more minutes until tender.
Mix [[2 tbsp]] flour with a little cold water to make a smooth paste, then stir into the stew.
Simmer 5 minutes until lightly thickened. Remove the thyme stems and hot pepper.
Serve in bowls, hot, with bread or dumplings.
Cut the breadfruit into quarters through the stem and cut out the tough core from each piece.
Peel off the green skin with a paring knife and cut the flesh into large chunks. Rub a little oil on your hands first, as the sap is sticky.
Bring [[8 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt to a boil in a large pot.
Add the breadfruit chunks and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until a fork slides in easily.
Drain well and let the steam escape for 2 minutes.
Toss the hot breadfruit with [[3 tbsp]] melted butter and [[0.25 tsp]] black pepper.
Serve warm as a side to fish or stews. For a roasted version, heat the oven to 400°F (200°C), roast the quartered unpeeled fruit for 1 hour until soft, then peel.

ing: about 8 inch squares; or use foil
st: Soften the banana leaves by passing each briefly over a gas flame or dipping in hot water. Cut into 8-inch squares.
In a large bowl, mix [[2 cups]] cornmeal, [[0.5 cup]] flour, [[0.75 cup]] brown sugar, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Stir in [[1 cup]] grated pumpkin, [[1 cup]] grated sweet potato, [[1 cup]] coconut and [[0.5 cup]] raisins.
Pour in [[4 tbsp]] melted butter and [[0.5 cup]] milk and mix into a thick, moist batter that drops from a spoon.
Spoon about [[0.33 cup]] batter onto the center of each leaf.
Fold the leaf over the filling into a flat parcel, tuck the ends under, and tie with kitchen string.
Set a steamer rack in a large pot with 2 inches of water and bring to a simmer.
Arrange the parcels on the rack, cover, and steam for 1 hour, topping up the water if needed.
Let cool for 10 minutes. Unwrap and eat warm; the conkie should be firm and set.
Whisk [[2 cups]] flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Rub in [[2 tbsp]] cold butter with your fingertips until crumbly.
Add [[0.5 cup]] cold water gradually, stirring until a soft dough forms. Add a spoonful more if dry.
Knead on a floured surface for 2 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and flatten each into a disc about 0.5 inch thick.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a deep skillet over medium heat to about 350°F (175°C), or until a pinch of dough sizzles.
Fry the cakes in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until puffed and deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with butter, jam or saltfish.
